lastText: File ClosedInsured Against a Question Nobody Could AnswerContestedThe War Cabinet and Chiefs of Staff, 1939–1945End of hostilities: NOVEMBER 1945 (PROJECTED) · filed late, out of sequenceImmediate AftermathVictory in Europe arrives around November 1945: slower than the historical May 1945, the price of caution at the moments this ████████ offered a faster, riskier road instead. The campaign reaches its end having spent more Western Allied lives than the historical record: the price of the bolder, more aggressive road at several of this campaign's genuine forks. Stalin was pressed hard on Poland's postwar government at Yalta rather than accepted on ambiguous terms: a harder line taken exactly where the historical conference chose accommodation. The Dieppe raid was cancelled: a division of mostly Canadian troops spared its ██████████ destruction, and the opposed-landing lessons that shaped Overlord's doctrine left to be learned later, more slowly, and possibly on the invasion beaches themselves. The stand in the Peloponnese held longer than the real withdrawal did, and the Navy lifted more men than the 50,732 that Operation Demon took off. No branch of this campaign ███████ a █████████ destination: the war's outcome was decided by arithmetic no single conference or campaign could overturn.One Year LaterA year past victory in Europe, the machinery of occupation is running on the arrangements this campaign's own conferences (Tehran, Yalta, the ones this command actually ████████)
